items.stem: Connecting with Geometry: ABC is an isosceles triangle in which AB = AC = 8 cm and BC = 12 cm. Find: First: $m(\angle B)$. Second: The area of the surface of the triangle to the nearest two decimal numbers.

items.caption: Isosceles triangle ABC with apex A, base CB; AB and AC each marked 8 cm; AD drawn perpendicular to CB with D on CB and right angle marked; CD = 6 cm, DB = 6 cm.

items.quote: Using the calculator :
items.text: Using the calculator: SHIFT cos 0.75 = ° ' '' ; $\therefore m(\angle B) = 41° 24' 35''$ (Q.E.D 1)

items.quote: To find the surface area of the triangle : find AD
items.text: To find the surface area of the triangle: find AD (From Pythagoras' theorem). $(AD)^2=(AB)^2-(BD)^2$; $(AD)^2 = 64-36=28$; $AD=2\sqrt{7}$. The area of the triangle ABC $=\frac12\times BC\times AD=\frac12\times 12\times 2\sqrt7 = 12\sqrt7$ cm$^2 \simeq 31.75$ cm$^2$ (Q.E.D. 2)
items.notes: Continues solution of previous example; 'Phythegoran's' misspelt in print.

items.quote: Another solution for the second part:
items.text: Another solution for the second part:

items.quote: sin B = AD/AB ... AD = 8 sin (41° 24' 35'')
items.text: $\because \sin B=\frac{AD}{AB}$, $\therefore \sin B=\frac{AD}{8}$, $\therefore AD = 8\sin(41°24'35'')$ (1). The area of the triangle ABC $=\frac12\times BC\times AD$, substitute from (1) in this relation: $\therefore$ area $=\frac12\times12\times8\sin(41°24'35'')\simeq 31.75$ cm$^2$.

learning_objectives.label: Ratios of 30°, 60°, 45°
learning_objectives.description: Determine the trigonometric ratios (sin, cos, tan) of the special angles 30°, 60° and 45° from the side ratios of an equilateral triangle and an isosceles right-angled triangle, and state that sin of an angle equals cos of its complementary angle.

learning_objectives.label: Evaluate special-angle expressions
learning_objectives.description: Evaluate and prove expressions involving the ratios of 30°, 45° and 60°, using exact values and the relations sin A = cos of the complementary angle and tan A = sin A / cos A.

learning_objectives.label: Ratios of angles by calculator
learning_objectives.description: Use a calculator to find the trigonometric ratio of a given angle, including angles in degrees, minutes and seconds.

learning_objectives.label: Find angle from its ratio
learning_objectives.description: Find the measure of an angle from its trigonometrical ratio, using the calculator or special-angle values, and apply this to find angles and areas in a triangle.
